label: Road rules
title: Road rules
headline: The rules people get wrong
intro: Test yourself on the Namibian road rules that drivers most often get wrong, from traffic circles to dead traffic lights.

scenes.question: What's the general speed limit on a public road inside a town in Namibia, unless a sign shows a lower one?

scenes.prompt: Compare the signals. Yellow means stop when you can do so safely; never accelerate to beat it.

art.alt: One traffic signal changing between off, red, yellow and green.

states.label: Off
states.caption: Treat a junction with dead signals as a four-way stop.

states.label: Yellow
states.caption: Stop if you can safely. Yellow does not mean accelerate.

states.label: Green
states.caption: Proceed only when the way is clear; watch for people crossing.

scenes.intro: Four everyday situations. What does the law say?

questions.line: You're coming up to a traffic circle. A car is already going around it from your right.

art.alt: Top-down view of a traffic circle.

questions.reason: At a traffic circle, yield to all traffic approaching from your right within the junction, unless a sign or officer says otherwise.

questions.line: The light ahead turns yellow. You're well back from the stop line.
questions.reason: A steady yellow means stop behind the line. Only carry on if you're so close that you can't stop safely.

questions.line: The power's out and the traffic lights at a junction are dark.
questions.prompt: How do you treat the junction?

options.label: The busier road has right of way

art.alt: A traffic light with all its lamps off.

questions.reason: When no light is working, every driver must act as at a three-way or four-way stop.

questions.line: Traffic is crawling. The shoulder is empty.
questions.prompt: You may drive on the shoulder to get past.

art.alt: Top-down view of a blue car in its lane beside a wide road shoulder.

questions.reason: You may not drive on the shoulder of a public road.

bands.title: Time for a refresher
bands.body: Some of these rules surprise a lot of drivers. Read the regulations, then try again.

bands.title: Getting there
bands.body: You know most of them. Check the ones you missed.

bands.title: Spot on
bands.body: You know the rules that most people get wrong.

scenes.explain: Inside a town, the general limit is {claim:na.law.speed-urban}, unless a sign shows a lower one.

lines: Yield to traffic already in the circle from your right.
Yellow means stop if you safely can.
Dead traffic lights: treat the junction as a four-way stop.

scenes.question: Drivers using a mobile phone are about how many times more likely to crash?

questions.line: Your phone rings while you're driving.

options.label: Hands-free, with the phone fixed or a headset
Holding it briefly at a red light

art.alt: A phone held in a dashboard holder.

questions.reason: You may not drive while holding a phone. You may only use it hands-free, fixed to the car or through a headset.

questions.line: You're following a car on the highway.

options.label: No closer than is reasonable for the speed, traffic and road

questions.reason: The law says no closer than is reasonable and prudent. As a guide, keep at least a {claim:int.uk.gap} gap, and double it on wet roads.

questions.line: Someone has stepped onto a zebra crossing on your half of the road.

art.alt: Top-down view of a pedestrian crossing with a refuge island.

questions.reason: Drivers must yield to a pedestrian on a crossing who is on their half of the road, or close to it.

questions.line: A bus has stopped and people are getting off.

art.alt: Side view of a stopped blue-and-white city bus with its passenger door open.

questions.reason: When passing a stationary bus, take care for people getting on or off, or walking to or from it.

bands.title: Time for a refresher
bands.body: Have another look at the ones you missed.

bands.title: Getting there
bands.body: Good, but check the ones you missed.

scenes.explain: Drivers using a phone are about {claim:int.who.phone} more likely to crash. In Namibia, holding a phone while driving is against the law.

lines: Phone out of your hand while you drive.
Leave a gap you could stop in.
People on foot first at crossings and around buses.
